Hi Eli / Sara,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a short term sheet (redwood-offer-term-sheet.docx) to make the tradeoffs explicit on the indemnity section so procurement has a concrete position to review. High level ask from Novella was that vendors take on defense for third-party IP claims — we understand why that’s important. A few specifics we want your confirmation on before legal starts final redlines: 

- Scoping: do you expect indemnity to cover claims arising from Novella’s internal models or customer-supplied data (training inputs)?
- Evidence & notice: what notice window is procurement requiring (we usually ask for 30 days written notice and an evidence packet)?
- Caps/insurance: can you confirm if Novella will accept a liability cap tied to fees/insurance offsets for third-party IP?

Initial Redwood stance we’d like to propose for discussion: 
- Redwood will defend and indemnify for third-party IP claims to the extent the claim arises from our model (i.e., model architecture or weights supplied by Redwood) or our pre-existing code. 
- We propose carveouts where Novella’s modifications, retraining on customer proprietary data, or deployments that alter the model chain remove Redwood’s defense obligation — in those cases we offer a reimbursement path.
- Notice + evidence: 30 days notice for claims where practicable, with an evidence checklist (we can provide a template).
- Counsel selection: Redwood to control defense unless a counsel conflict is shown; material settlements above threshold require mutual consent.

We’ve got a procurement review on Wednesday and it would be helpful to get Novella’s redlines or comments before then. Can you either: 1) send your marked-up MSA (PDF is fine), or 2) confirm a short call tomorrow morning to align?

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to run through.

Ben / Marissa — saw Eli's redlines. Below are practical positions we can take in the near term so sales/procurement can converge quickly. I've attached our evidence checklist template (RDW_evidence_template.xlsx) for Novella to complete in the event of a claim.

Suggested compromise (short bullets you can share):
1) Scope: Redwood will defend and indemnify Novella for third-party IP infringement claims to the extent the claim arises from: (a) Redwood-delivered model weights or model code, or (b) Redwood-hosted prebuilt connectors/plugins.
2) Carveout for customer-driven retraining / modifications: If Novella materially alters the model (retraining that changes model behavior) or injects customer-proprietary prompts/data that directly cause the asserted infringement, Redwood's indemnity is limited to reimbursement for documented direct losses (reimburse path).
3) Notice & evidence: Novella must give written notice promptly and provide the RDW evidence checklist within 10 business days of notice. We can accept 10 business days if the checklist is met; otherwise the parties will work in good faith to provide additional evidence in a rolling fashion.
4) Defense control: Redwood to control defense with counsel of Redwood's choice. If Novella reasonably demonstrates a conflict of interest, parties will agree on independent counsel. Significant settlements or admissions (over $100k) require mutual written consent.
5) Cap & insurance: Liability cap equal to the greater of (a) the fees paid in prior 12 months or (b) $1,000,000. Redwood confirms it carries Third Party IP coverage; settlement recoveries shall be net of insurance proceeds unless otherwise agreed.
6) Escrow / holdback: as a procurement concession, propose a 6-month holdback of 10% of the first-year committed fees to be released on successful PO issuance and account activation — this is optional but gives procurement comfort without increasing the cap.

Fallback positions to have in the call: 
- If Novella insists on full defend-and-control with no carveouts, propose splitting by claim type (patent vs. copyright) with narrower defense for training-related claims.
- If they insist on <10 business days for evidence, accept 5 business days for initial acknowledgment but keep 10 days for full evidence packet.

I'll join any call with procurement or their counsel. If they send a marked redline, send to me and I will produce clean language for the MSA.
